summary: Frontend colour-pass verification of Statement Detail on web + mobile. Login as cathy@example.com worked; opened statement 673fa982-... on both surfaces. Web: layout (Rights redesigned as cards, AI accuracy banner at bottom, no decoder-format-disclaimer at top, stream headers solid teal + white text in LIGHT) is correct, BUT the requested clay/teal/sage tinted backgrounds on statement-notes-card, statement-ask-wayly-card, statement-rights-panel and decoder-balance-panel are NOT applied — the class names in the JSX (`sect-clay-soft`, `sect-teal-soft`, `sect-sage-soft`) do not exist in the CSS (only `.section-*-soft` and `.sect-*` without the `-soft` suffix exist). computed backgroundColor is rgba(0,0,0,0) on all four cards. Dark mode: stream card headers turn clay (rgb 165,81,43) instead of teal — appears to be a `bg-primary-k` dark-swap. Mobile: goldSoft/sageSoft tokens exist and apply, but `colors.primarySoft` is UNDEFINED in the theme (neither `theme/tokens.ts` nor `theme/palette.ts` defines primarySoft/tealSoft), so summary-card renders untinted (falls back to Card default). This mobile branch is broken.

ui_bugs.issue: className `sect-clay-soft` does not exist in CSS; card renders with transparent bg — no clay tint. Fix: rename CSS or use existing `.section-clay-soft` (index.css:260) or `.sect-clay` (index.css:1454).
className `sect-teal-soft` not defined — no teal tint applied.
className `sect-clay-soft` not defined — panel container has no clay tint (the inner right-* cards do get their border-l-clay accent correctly).
className `sect-sage-soft` not defined — panel renders transparent instead of sage tint.

In DARK mode, stream-card header bg becomes clay rgb(165,81,43) instead of the required SOLID TEAL. `bg-primary-k` is being remapped to clay in the dark theme. Spec asks for teal header in both modes.

issues: All four requested tinted surfaces (notes, ask, rights, balance) render as page-background off-white — the intended colour pass is not visually present.

ui_bugs.issue: `colors.primarySoft` is undefined in theme (theme/tokens.ts and theme/palette.ts have `primary`, `goldSoft`, `sageSoft` but NO `primarySoft`/`tealSoft`). backgroundColor resolves to undefined → summary-card renders without the requested teal-soft tint.
OK — colors.goldSoft (#F3E7DE) resolves and applies a gold/clay-soft tint as expected.

issues: Test statement 673fa982... uses decoded (audit_json) branch on mobile so legacy cards were not shown for that id; token audit against colors object shows primarySoft is missing regardless of statement content.

parity_issues.expected: notes=clay-soft, ask=teal-soft, rights=clay-soft, balance=sage-soft on web; summary=teal-soft on mobile.

action_items: Add missing CSS: `.sect-clay-soft`, `.sect-teal-soft`, `.sect-sage-soft` classes to /app/frontend/src/index.css (or update JSX to use existing `.section-*-soft` classes at index.css:259-261). Preferred: add `-soft` variants of `.sect-*` matching the design tokens.

Add missing mobile theme token `primarySoft` (e.g. '#E4EEEF' or color-mix teal 9% on surface) in /app/mobile/theme/tokens.ts AND lightColors/darkColors in /app/mobile/theme/palette.ts. Update summary-card to use the correct token.

critical_code_review_comments: CSS class naming is inconsistent: `.sect-*` (dark, inset accent), `.section-*-soft` (subtle tint) — the JSX uses a third variant `.sect-*-soft` that exists nowhere. Consolidate to a single naming convention across CSS + JSX.
Mobile theme token surface should mirror web tokens 1:1 (comment in palette.ts explicitly says so). Missing `primarySoft` breaks that mirror.
Consider a lint rule / unit test that fails if a JSX className string references an undefined Tailwind/utility class, to prevent future silent misses like this.

rca of the issue: Web: class names `sect-clay-soft`/`sect-teal-soft`/`sect-sage-soft` used in StatementNotes.jsx:59, StatementAskWayly.jsx:87, StatementRightsPanel.jsx:25, DecoderResultView.jsx:528 do not exist in /app/frontend/src/index.css. CSS defines `.section-*-soft` (lines 259-261, subtle tint) and `.sect-*` (lines 1453-1461, stronger accent with inset shadow) but NOT `.sect-*-soft`. Because Tailwind purges unused CSS but does not error on unknown classes, the mismatch silently rendered transparent. Mobile: /app/mobile/theme/tokens.ts exports `colors` and /app/mobile/theme/palette.ts exports `lightColors`/`darkColors`; neither defines `primarySoft`, so `colors.primarySoft` on statement/[id].tsx:263 evaluates to undefined. Reproduction: log in as cathy, open /app/statements/{any-id}, inspect getComputedStyle for the four data-testids listed — backgroundColor === 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)'.
